external_effects: navigates and interacts with arbitrary websites through a real browser
can submit forms, click controls, upload files and trigger site-side mutations
can download files and write screenshots, PDFs, snapshots, traces and videos
can read, set, clear, persist and restore cookies and browser storage state
can attach to existing browser profiles or CDP endpoints
can run arbitrary Playwright code and grant browser permissions
can call page-provided WebMCP tools whose effects are controlled by the page
can globally install or update @playwright/cli through npm
can attach generated browser evidence to GitHub pull requests through gh commands

reviewed_subcapabilities.rationale: The documented install command copies skills into workspace or home-directory agent skill locations.
Core browser actions can change external application state and upload local files.
Snapshots, screenshots, requests and console inspection are useful but still expose page data and can write local artifacts.
The skill can inspect, mutate, persist, restore and delete cookies and browser storage, including authenticated state.
run-code evaluates arbitrary Playwright functions with browser-context access, permissions and file-download capabilities.
Page-registered WebMCP tools are explicitly untrusted and may have remote side effects when called.
Attaching to existing browsers or persistent profiles can expose authenticated sessions and unrelated browsing state.
Route/unroute commands alter browser network behavior and can materially change application behavior under test.
Generation and healing workflows can write or modify test code based on browser interactions.
The skill can generate visual artifacts and instruct attaching them to GitHub pull requests, crossing a publication boundary.
The skill instructs global installation of the latest CLI when unavailable locally.

narrower_admission_candidates.condition: Consider only isolated-session navigation, snapshots and read-only inspection with uploads, storage mutation, arbitrary code, WebMCP calls, persistent profiles and attached browsers disabled.
Consider local test diagnostics when browser access is isolated, test execution is already authorized, and no external site mutation or code rewriting occurs.

rationale: Official Microsoft provenance and strong browser-automation guidance are established, but the skill grants broad Bash-backed browser control, global package installation, authenticated storage access, arbitrary Playwright code, file upload/download, page-provided WebMCP calls and external publication/mutation surfaces. Package-level automatic admission is too broad.
